title: Chopok Both Sides: A Jasná Week with the High Tatras Attached
subRegion: Nízke Tatry (Demänovská dolina and Chopok Juh) with the High Tatras at Tatranská Lomnica and Štrbské Pleso

bestPeriod.window: late January to mid-March — the coldest, deepest, most reliable stretch on both aspects of Chopok
bestPeriod.avoid: the Slovak and Polish school holidays in early February (queues at the Funitel) and after mid-April

accommodation.note: €420–€700 (€60–€100/night; Demänovská dolina chalet or Liptovský Mikuláš base)

transport.note: €230–€360 (hire car 7 days, fuel, motorway e-známka, TEŽ tickets)

activities.note: €430–€620 (5–6 ski days on GOPASS, one guided free-ride day, one thermal afternoon)

hook: Chopok is a bald 2,024 m dome with a resort hanging off each side of it, and the whole week turns on which way the wind is blowing. North into Demänovská dolina you get glacial cirques, the Funitel, and free-ride terrain that would be roped off in Austria. South you get sun and shelter when the north is shut. Add two days in the High Tatras for the Lomnické sedlo couloir and a hot pool at the end. Cold, serious, and cheaper than it should be.

snapshot.Start / End: Poprad or Bratislava → Demänovská dolina (5 nights) → Tatranská Lomnica (2 nights) → Poprad
snapshot.Getting there: Poprad-Tatry (TAT) is 70 km east of Jasná, about an hour on the D1; Bratislava (BTS) is 300 km, 3 h; Kraków (KRK) is 200 km north over the border. Rail: the InterCity to Liptovský Mikuláš, then bus or taxi 12 km up Demänovská dolina.

itinerary.title: Arrival and the Lower Mountain (Biela púť 950 → Priehyba 1,500 m)
itinerary.morning: Land at Poprad-Tatry, collect the car, and drive the D1 west to Liptovský Mikuláš, then 12 km up **Demänovská dolina**.
itinerary.afternoon: Half-day pass and the **Záhradky/Priehyba** sector to get calibrated — wide, north-facing, tree-lined, forgiving.
itinerary.evening: Check in, then dinner at **Koliba Bystrina** in the valley: bryndzové halušky, grilled trout, and a shot of borovička you will regret at 07:00 [VERIFY: current koliba opening hours].

itinerary.title: Chopok North to South and Back
itinerary.morning: First lift, straight up through Luková to the **Funitel** and over the summit before the crowd. Check the wind forecast the night before; if the Funitel is closed, this day becomes Day 3.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to **Chopok Juh** via the **Rotunda**, ski the Kosodrevina and Srdiečko runs in the sun, and eat at the **Rotunda** restaurant on the summit itself.
itinerary.evening: Back over the top by 15:00 at the latest — miss the last summit lift and you are paying for a taxi round the massif. Drinks at the **Von Roll bar** at Biela púť, built into old lift machinery.

itinerary.title: Free Ride Day: Zadné Dery and Kotlová (guided, avalanche kit mandatory)
itinerary.morning: Meet your guide, do a transceiver drill in the car park, and read the **SLP** bulletin together. Then into the **Zadné Dery** cirque — the classic Jasná free-ride line, north-facing, holding cold snow for days after a storm.
itinerary.afternoon: **Kotlová** if the rating allows, or a mellower flank if it does not. Guides turn these days around routinely and you should let them.
itinerary.evening: Recovery at **Tatralandia** in Liptovský Mikuláš, 20 minutes down the valley — thermal water, outdoor pools, steam at −10 °C.

itinerary.title: South Side Full Day and Kamenná Chata
itinerary.morning: Drive round to **Srdiečko** on the south side (about 1 h from Demänovská dolina) or take the interconnect if it is running. South-facing spring snow softens by 10:30.
itinerary.afternoon: Skin or ride up to **Kamenná chata pod Chopkom** at around 1,740 m for soup and the ridge view — the most atmospheric lunch on the mountain.
itinerary.evening: Relocate east, or stay and eat in the valley; if you are moving to the High Tatras, do it tonight so tomorrow starts on the lift.

itinerary.title: Tatranská Lomnica and Lomnické sedlo (Skalnaté pleso 1,751 m → Lomnické sedlo 2,190 m)
itinerary.morning: Cable car from **Tatranská Lomnica** to **Skalnaté pleso**, then the small cabin to **Lomnické sedlo** — the steepest lift-served slope in Slovakia, unpisted at the top and closed outright in high avalanche danger.
itinerary.afternoon: Long runs back down to the village through the forest, then the separate cable car to **Lomnický štít** (2,634 m) if you have booked it: a hard quota, fixed time slots, a limited number of passengers per cabin and a set time at the summit [VERIFY: current Lomnický štít quota, slot rules and fare].
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Tatranská Lomnica; the Grandhotel Praha's dining room is the old-Tatras option.

itinerary.title: Štrbské Pleso and the Electric Railway (1,346 m lake, Solisko 1,840 m)
itinerary.morning: Take the **Tatranská elektrická železnica** — the narrow-gauge electric tramway linking Poprad, Starý Smokovec, Tatranská Lomnica and Štrbské Pleso — rather than driving. Ski the **Solisko** chair above the lake.
itinerary.afternoon: The frozen **Štrbské Pleso** itself, the ski-jump towers, and the cross-country trails that hosted the 1970 Nordic World Championships; hire skate skis for an hour if the alpine legs are gone.
itinerary.evening: Back by TEŽ. A last Tatra dinner and an early night — the drive west starts tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Last Turns, Thermal Water, and Out
itinerary.morning: Either a final half-day at Lomnica or a straight run west on the D1 to **Bešeňová** (Gino Paradise), the Liptov thermal complex 20 km from Jasná [VERIFY: current Bešeňová opening hours and admission].
itinerary.afternoon: Hot water, then Poprad or Bratislava. Allow an hour Bešeňová → Poprad, three hours to Bratislava.
itinerary.evening: Fly out. If the flight is late, the **Demänovská ľadová jaskyňa** ice cave is closed in winter, but Liptovský Mikuláš's old square is a decent hour.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Tri Studničky
accommodationStrategy.description: timber-built, at the foot of the valley road with the ski bus stopping outside, a proper drying room, and a pool for the evening of a free-ride day. Closest thing to ski-in convenience without the Biela púť car-park noise.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 8–12 weeks ahead for February; direct rates usually beat the aggregators [VERIFY: current rates].

accommodationStrategy.name: Chalets Jasná Collection
accommodationStrategy.description: self-catering apartments a short walk from the base lifts and the Von Roll, with ski storage and boot heaters. The right choice for a group of four to six splitting an avalanche-kit hire and a guide.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 10–14 weeks ahead for peak weeks; ask which building is nearest the Záhradky lift.

accommodationStrategy.name: Grandhotel Praha
accommodationStrategy.description: 1905 spa-hotel bones, three minutes from the Lomnica cable car station, so the Day 5 first-lift plan needs no car. Good for the two-night High Tatras block.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6–10 weeks ahead; ask for a room facing Lomnický štít.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming applies; 4G is solid in Demänovská dolina and across the Tatra villages, unreliable in the Zadné Dery cirque. Download offline maps and the avalanche bulletin before you go up.
logistics.emergency: 112, and **HZS mountain rescue on 18 300** — save it. Rescue in Slovakia is chargeable to the person rescued, so mountain-sports insurance covering off-piste and helicopter evacuation is not optional here.
logistics.weather: the Tatras get severe wind. Summit lifts and the Chopok interconnect close regularly, sometimes for days, and the Lomnický štít cable car is the first to stop. Build every plan with a south-side or tree-line fallback.
logistics.bookingWindows: GOPASS passes at least a week ahead for the discount tier; guides 3–4 weeks; Lomnický štít slots as far ahead as the system allows; hotels 8–14 weeks for February.
logistics.money: Slovakia uses the **euro**, so no conversion at all — one of the quiet advantages over the Polish side. Cards work everywhere including mountain restaurants; carry €20 in coins for lockers and the TEŽ machines. Polish złoty is needed only if you cross for the Tatry Super Ski option.
logistics.transportRules: motorways require an **e-známka** vignette bought online by plate; roughly €12 for 10 days [VERIFY: current e-známka tariff]. **Winter tyres are compulsory when there is compacted snow or ice on the road**, and Demänovská dolina qualifies most of the winter. The valley road is steep and can require chains. Slovakia enforces a **0.00 blood-alcohol limit** for drivers.
logistics.permits: no permits for skiing, but the High Tatras sit inside **TANAP** national park with a seasonal closure of most marked hiking trails from **1 November to 15 June**; ski touring is restricted to permitted routes, and the Free Ride zones at Jasná are governed by daily gate decisions, not by your own judgement.

proTips: Buy GOPASS days **online, in your account, at least seven days ahead**. The window-price gap is the largest single saving on this trip, and it costs nothing but planning.
Watch the wind forecast for Chopok, not the snow forecast. The interconnect is the week's biggest variable, and a 60 km/h gusting day means a south-side plan made the night before.
On a storm day, ski **Záhradky** and the lower Priehyba trees. Visibility on the bald upper bowl goes to nothing, and the tree-line is where Jasná's best storm skiing is anyway.
Take the **Tatranská elektrická železnica** between the High Tatras villages rather than driving. Parking at Štrbské Pleso and Tatranská Lomnica fills by 09:00 in February; the tram does not.
Book **Lomnický štít** before you leave home. It runs on a hard quota with timed slots, and turning up hoping for a cabin is how people miss it entirely.
Do an avalanche day, not just a guided day. **SLP** and **JAMES** run short courses out of Jasná, and a two-day course plus a free-ride day costs less than three lift days in the Alps.
Finish at **Bešeňová** rather than Tatralandia if you want quiet. Tatralandia is the family water park; Bešeňová is the hot pools, and on a Tuesday afternoon it is nearly empty.

raw.Lift pass pricing and the GOPASS system: Jasná and the Tatra resorts sell through **GOPASS**, which is a loyalty account, not just a webshop. Prices are **dynamic**: the same day costs less the earlier you buy it online, with tiered discounts that shrink as the date approaches and vanish at the ticket window. A 1-day adult Jasná pass in high season sits broadly in the €55–€72 band depending on how far ahead you buy, with multi-day passes cheaper per day and a range of season products (including a full-season pass valid across the group's Slovak resorts) [VERIFY: 2026/27 tariff and GOPASS discount tiers]. Two rules that always hold: register the account and buy at least a week ahead, and load the pass onto a reusable keycard rather than paying the deposit again each morning.
raw.The Tatry Super Ski alternative: For a Poland-side crossover week there is a separate regional pass covering **15 Polish and 4 Slovak resorts** — roughly **118 runs, 84 km of piste and 100+ lifts**. Indicative prices: **1-day 150–185 PLN**, 2-day 285–350, 3-day 410–510, **7-day 835–1,055 PLN**, and a 14-day flexible at **1,799 PLN**, season-dependent — about €35–€43 for a day and €194–€245 for the week at roughly 4.3 PLN to €1 [VERIFY: current PLN exchange rate]. Important: the **Kasprowy Wierch cable car is not covered** and needs a separate ticket, though the Kasprowy chairlifts are included on multi-day passes. This pass does **not** include Jasná — treat it as an alternative week, not a supplement.
raw.Lift network and interconnects: **Chopok** (2,024 m) is the hinge. On the north side, Jasná rises from **Biela púť** and **Záhradky** through the **Priehyba** and **Luková** sectors; the **Funitel** — a twin-cable gondola built to run in wind that stops ordinary lifts — carries you from Luková to the summit. Over the top, the **Rotunda** cable car drops to **Kosodrevina** and **Srdiečko** on **Chopok Juh**, the south side, which is a genuinely different mountain: sunnier, more sheltered, quieter. The interconnect is the whole point of the ski area and the first thing to fail in a storm; if the Funitel and Rotunda are wind-held, the two sides are 90 minutes apart by road.
raw.Snow reliability: Jasná is the most snow-sure resort in the wider Carpathians: a north-facing main bowl of **glacial cirques** holding wind-blown snow well into spring, a top station at 2,000 m, and a south side that keeps skiing when the north is scoured. Snowmaking covers the valley runs down to Biela púť. Practical consequence: in a thaw, ski north; in a gale, ski south; in a storm, ski the trees at Záhradky.
raw.Free Ride zones and their rules: Jasná marks official **Free Ride zones** — **Zadné Dery** and **Kotlová** are the names to know, plus terrain off the south side. They are unpatrolled, unsecured and not avalanche-controlled: entry means transceiver, shovel and probe, a partner, and reading the day's bulletin from the **Stredisko lavínovej prevencie** (the Slovak avalanche prevention centre, based in Jasná). Gates close when the danger rating rises. Guiding and avalanche courses run through **UIAGM/IFMGA-qualified Slovak mountain guides** and through **SLP** and **JAMES** (the Slovak mountaineering association) programmes [VERIFY: current guide day rates and course dates]. Rescue is **Horská záchranná služba (HZS)** on **18 300**.
